lines: Jordan Rivera
+1 (555) 010-2287 | jordan.rivera@example.com | example.com/in/jrivera
EDUCATION
Northgate University | M.P.H. in Biostatistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Northgate University Hospital | Research Assistant | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Aug 2022
- Randomized patients by assigning those admitted on odd-numbered days to the program and even-numbered days to usual care.
- Interviewed 25 patients about missed clinic visits; the findings added text reminders that cut no-shows from 18% to 11%.
- Wrote the study's data dictionary for 180 variables, which the next two cohort studies reused.

- Cleaned and merged lab data from two hospital systems while also scheduling participant visits, ordering study supplies, taking minutes at lab meetings and covering the front desk, which resolved 1,200 mismatched patient identifiers.
Meridian Heart Institute | Clinical Research Coordinator | Metro City, USA | Sep 2022 - Jul 2025
- Coordinated a 3-site randomized trial of a nurse-led discharge program for 640 heart-failure patients, finishing enrollment 4 months early with 94% of follow-up visits completed.
- Cut data-entry errors in the trial database from 6.1% to 1.8% of fields by adding range checks and double entry for the primary outcome.
- Estimated median survival in each arm by averaging the follow-up time of patients who died, excluding censored patients.
- Reconciling adverse-event reports across three sites, coding them to MedDRA terms and cross-checking them against pharmacy records each week, cut unresolved safety queries from 45 to 6.
- Presented monthly safety reports to the data monitoring committee, and all 4 reviews passed without a protocol change.
- Trained 9 site nurses on the consent process and outcome forms, and no consent deviations were found at the final audit.
PROJECTS
Asthma Readmission Analysis | Independent Project | R | Jan 2025 - Present
- Harnessed cutting-edge analytics to deliver transformative, patient-centered insights into respiratory health outcomes.
- Found that 7-day follow-up cut readmission from 12% to 8%, a 50% reduction, after adjusting for age and insurance.
- Raised the survey response rate by 20% with SMS reminders, from 35% to 55% of invited residents.
Community Health Survey | Volunteer, Team of 5 | REDCap | Mar 2020 - Aug 2020
- Designed a 30-question community health survey and collected 1,100 responses, giving the clinic its first estimate of uninsured residents by neighborhood.
- The survey was translated into Spanish and piloted with 20 residents before launch.
- Wrote the survey's data codebook, which the clinic used for its follow-up survey the next year.
SKILLS
Tools: R, REDCap
Methods: randomized trials, regression, mixed-effects models, survey design

items.says: Make the profile link a working, professional link rather than a placeholder.
Put Meridian Heart Institute before Northgate University Hospital.
items.because: Reverse chronological order makes your progression easier to follow.

items.says: Odd/even admission-day assignment is not randomized.
items.because: It is predictable assignment, not random allocation.

items.says: Clarify your role in developing or implementing the reminders.
items.because: As written, the bullet credits the interviews alone with reducing no-shows.

items.says: Say whether the 18%–11% change was measured before and after implementation.
items.because: The timing of the measured change is unclear.

items.says: Separate or cut the administrative tasks.
items.because: The identifier-reconciliation result will stand out more.

items.says: Clarify how many identifiers your cleaning and merging work resolved.
items.because: The current list makes the connection to the result hard to see.

items.says: Verify that “randomized” accurately describes the trial.
Verify the intended denominators for the enrollment and follow-up figures.
Averaging follow-up time among patients who died does not estimate median survival.
Identify the method actually used if you performed a valid censored-survival analysis.
Make the verb tense consistent with a completed role.
Clarify your contribution to the drop in unresolved safety queries.
Replace or substantiate “reviews passed” by explaining what the committee reviewed or what deliverable you owned.
items.because: Absence of a protocol change is not necessarily a measure of report quality.

items.says: Specify the audit scope if “no consent deviations” applies only to particular sites or records.
Replace the broad “cutting-edge analytics” claim with the actual dataset, methods, or output.
items.because: It gives a reviewer nothing to assess.

items.says: The 50% reduction is incorrect.
items.because: A drop from 12% to 8% is 4 percentage points, or about 33% relative.

items.says: Avoid implying that follow-up caused the decrease if the analysis was observational.
items.because: The adjustment does not establish causation.

items.says: Calling the change from 35% to 55% a 20% increase misstates the metric.
items.because: It is 20 percentage points, or about a 57% relative increase.

items.says: Clarify whether the survey belongs to the asthma project.
items.because: “Invited residents” otherwise seems disconnected from readmissions.

items.says: Add a clinic decision informed by the uninsured estimate if you can verify one.
items.because: It would show an outcome of the estimate.

items.says: Clarify your role in the translation and pilot.
items.because: The work is left entirely passive.

items.says: List only methods you can discuss and substantiate in the experience or projects.
items.because: The survival-analysis bullet needs resolving before you present trial-analysis expertise.
